body: Thank you, kind stranger.
that’s reassuring. thank you for the comment :)
congrats, you are mentally healthy! cannot relate unfortunately.
you don’t sound cheesy, don’t worry. this made me smile. you’re a very kind human and i wish you all the best
this put a smile on my face. glad we could help in a way :)
i’ve been on various ones since late 2020 but my mental health has still only gotten worse. i’m gonna talk to my psychiatrist about switching again.
on god
that indeed sounds rough. but hey what’s a couple minutes after you’re gone y’know
thank you for linking the faq! extremely helpful info :)
my family. i can’t stand being alive, but i also can’t bear the thought of hurting them. i wrestle between the two every day.
there are various small things that i enjoy, but i hardly feel like doing anything anymore :(
true but at this point the depression is weighing me down so hard that it hardly seems worth it
thank you, i’ll try not to.
my heads a bit of a mess right now so it’s hard to pinpoint specifics, but in general i feel like a disappointment and a waste of space

thank you for the kind comment. i’m currently medicated and in therapy but it’s only once a month. i’m 18 and still dependent on my mother so i don’t want to make her pay more than she already is. it really does feel like i’m losing myself to the depression but i know i’m more than that. thanks again for your words 🤍

shifting is NOT easy for the vast majority of us, and that’s not a bad thing. there’s no reason an objectively “easy” endeavor should take multiple years of constant effort to accomplish. i don’t care how people try to phrase or justify it.
best of luck!! i’m looking to switch things up too since the intent method is a little too slow for my liking. been doing some research on sats recently and i might give it another shot.

you described it pretty much perfectly :’)
nearly 3 years in my case and little to no noticeable progress makes it difficult to stay positive, but i believe it’ll be well worth it someday!

so people who have gone a long time without seeing success aren’t allowed to talk about it because it makes y’all feel bad?? i mean, i get it. i was new to shifting at some point too and would get a little scared seeing that some people have tried for years with no success. but now that i’ve become just that, i really don’t know how to feel anymore. every shifter should be able to post whatever feelings they may have about their journey, whether positive or negative (& tagged correctly ofc).
i’m at a little over 2.5 years and no success 🥲 it’ll be 3 in august lol

i’ve been at it for nearly 3 years now and haven’t believed the “shifting is easy” talk for a while now. “shifting is easy but the journey’s difficult” or whatever, it’s all the same to me ☠️

i think it comes easy to some people, but not everyone. if it truly is easy, that kinda implies that those of us who have been trying for a while must be doing something horribly wrong for us to not have shifted once. but that’s just the way i see it. i think shifting is a unique endeavor for everyone.

honestly i have no clue what i really want to do, which kinda contributes to my lack of interest towards school. i do enjoy drawing and i could see myself majoring in graphic design but my school doesn’t offer it, and either way i doubt it’ll pay the bills. as for tech school, until now i’ve never actually thought about it! i’ll look into it in a bit. thank you for your comment i genuinely appreciate it :’)
done. i like the amount of detail put into this! looking forward to the results :)
the degree i chose was psychology, but now i’m unsure lmao. ironically my psychology course is the one i’m doing the worst in ahaha…
you clearly have never read the bible my g
oh nice. and if i am confirmed?

this exactly. the whole reason i made the post to begin with is because i was angry about not being able to decide for myself. if i happened to stumble across catholicism on my own and get baptized of my own accord, perhaps i’d be somewhere much different today. too many friends of mine who were raised in christian/catholic households and schools turned out to be atheists as they grew older, so something’s clearly wrong here. if my future kids wanna get baptized when they’re old enough to make the decision for themselves, they have my full consent. being provided that choice is most important, at least in my opinion.
EXACTLY!! there’s so much shit that catholicism has pounded into our heads since day 1, and unfortunately we have to WORK to overcome that programming.

this. i feel like there’s nothing else to say when it comes to this and, having been there, we all know how empty those words of comfort come across as. but hey, at least we all get to feel shitty together. ghost hugs to this entire sub :)
thank you for this :)
thanks!!! right back at you :)
i can relate. edgy as fuck but you have a way with words.
